db_semantics: The ordinary insert_on/replace_on path still selects the original one-row dependency writer. Only existing full-snapshot snapshot_leaf_batches selects replace_snapshot_on, and batching requires at least eight normalized dependencies.

Manifest clone, normalization, validation, JSON size check, dependency DELETE, manifest INSERT/digest and subsequent table order remain in the same sequence. Public-surface validation/insertion remains before dependency replacement.

The normalized BTreeSet is borrowed directly. No whole-file vector, cross-file mixing, row reordering or additional deduplication is introduced. Bindings remain file_path/kind.as_str/key in that order.

Existing tiers 64/8/1 and bounds of at most 64 borrowed rows and 64 KiB actual bound-value payload are reused. Repeated file_path bytes are counted for each row. A legal oversized single row retains the one-row path; this is not an RSS cap or a new row-rejection threshold.

Generalizing bounded_rows from slices to IntoIterator retains exact-size slice behavior for all six existing callers. Empty upper bound and capacity lower bound affect allocation only for the concrete slice/BTreeSet iterators used.

SQL errors propagate through the existing owned temporary rebuild. Failed staging cannot publish new live rows or generation. Statement-level partial staging contents may differ; no physical rollback claim is made for journal-OFF staging.

New failure/parity controls compare original writer with snapshot writer, rowid/order/manifests/surfaces, generation changes, ordinary incremental replacement, injected key-70 ABORT and invalid manifest 999. Existing FTS rebuild opt-in and transaction/publication seam are preserved.
oracle_semantics: One RowProjection exists per immutable column layout, table and input side; map keys/nodes are reused, while values are released to null after serialization and on projection failure.

All five ValueRef conversions are unchanged, including strict UTF-8 rejection and original BLOB digest. Integer extrema, signed zero, Unicode/control characters, NULL and empty-BLOB values have literal expected JSON controls.

serialize_row returns an owned String before clearing values. The legacy project_row wrapper still returns an owned Value::Object. Existing ordering behavior, including a preserve_order build, follows the same insertion order.

Streaming row-count and raw row-size checks precede projection. Serialized/cumulative-byte limits, checked arithmetic, ordinals, duplicate retention, sorting, fifteen-table set and canonical SQL spool batches are unchanged.

reference_spool now calls the same changed project_row, so that comparison alone is not independent evidence of conversion equivalence. The added literal expected-value tests and invalid-UTF8 partial-update/recovery control address this limitation; they remain pending actual execution.
No measured allocation, RSS, runtime or 100k speedup is claimed.
